disclaimer: Fictional synthetic exemplars for drafting practice only. No real student data. Not legal advice.

exemplars.title: Grade 6 — SLD, reading comprehension in content areas
exemplars.profile_summary: A sixth-grade student who decodes on grade level but comprehends content-area text at 50%, struggles with text structure and academic vocabulary, and cannot independently summarize textbook sections.
strengths: Strong verbal participation in class discussion
Good note-taking when given a template
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent worries about the student's grades dropping as textbooks get harder and asks how to help at home.
evaluation_data: Reading comprehension: 50% on grade-6 content-area passages
Academic vocabulary: 55% on curriculum vocabulary probes
Text structure knowledge: needs direct instruction (identified in evaluation)
Decoding and fluency within grade-level expectations

plaafp.academic: The student reads grade-6 text fluently but earns 50% on comprehension questions, misidentifies text structures, and uses academic vocabulary accurately in only 55% of opportunities. Independent summaries omit central ideas and include irrelevant details.
plaafp.functional: The student reads assignments but cannot extract what matters, leading to incomplete homework and low quiz scores; becomes discouraged when asked to 'study' without a structured method.
plaafp.impact: Comprehension and vocabulary deficits related to the specific learning disability interfere with all content-area learning and require explicit strategy instruction with scaffolded text.

goals.area: Reading comprehension — text structure and main idea
goals.condition: Given grade-6 content-area text and a text-structure graphic organizer
goals.skill: identify text structure, main idea, and supporting evidence

goals.condition: Given explicit vocabulary instruction and practice across content areas
goals.skill: define and use grade-6 academic vocabulary in context
goals.measurement: Bi-weekly vocabulary probes; application in writing

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; progress reports include check scores and samples of summaries.
supplementary_aids_services: Access to audiobooks/digital text with adjustable text size
accommodations: Extended time on reading and assessment tasks
Read-aloud of directions and non-target test items
Chunked reading assignments with checkpoint questions
Option to respond orally or use speech-to-text
personnel_supports: Cross-team training on content literacy strategies
Shared vocabulary list protocol for all teachers
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is included in all general education classes and receives SDI in a resource setting for explicit comprehension strategy instruction. Pull-out is necessary for modeled strategy practice and immediate feedback; strategies are applied in content classes with organizer supports.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and all district assessments with extended time, chunking, and permitted read-aloud of directions. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed a pattern of comprehension-strategy regression over the prior summer with slow recoupment; ESY reading comprehension 2x/week, 45 minutes for 5 weeks is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
source_lineage: Missouri DESE PLAAFP and SMART Goal rubrics
exemplars.notes: Transition prompts should stay inactive below grade 9/age 16; the tool should display the trigger rule.

exemplars.title: Grade 7 — SLD, math reasoning (ratios, proportions, pre-algebra)
exemplars.profile_summary: A seventh-grade student who computes accurately but cannot set up proportional relationships or solve multi-step pre-algebra problems, scoring 35% on applied reasoning tasks.
strengths: Accurate with basic operations and integers
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is concerned the student may not be ready for algebra and wants to know what supports will continue next year.
evaluation_data: Applied math reasoning: 35% on grade-7 tasks
Algebraic representation: needs direct instruction with equations and tables
Evaluation confirmed SLD in math reasoning

plaafp.academic: The student computes accurately (90%) but solves applied ratio/proportion and pre-algebra problems at 35%; struggles to translate words into equations and to choose between additive and multiplicative reasoning.
plaafp.functional: The student avoids multi-step problems, tries to calculate quickly, and does not check whether answers are reasonable; benefits from structured planning and estimation routines.
plaafp.impact: Math-reasoning deficits related to the specific learning disability limit access to grade-7 standards and preparedness for algebra, requiring explicit reasoning and representation instruction.

goals.condition: Given grade-7 ratio/proportion tasks, tables, and graphs
goals.skill: represent and solve proportional relationships using equations and reasoning
goals.target: 80% correct across 3 of 4 consecutive weekly probes
goals.measurement: Weekly curriculum-based reasoning probes with rubric

goals.condition: Given a word problem and a translation template
goals.skill: write an equation or expression that models the situation and solve it

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with probe data and work samples.
supplementary_aids_services: Reference cards for steps and formulas
accommodations: Extended time on math tasks and assessments
Read-aloud of word problems when reading is not the target
Calculator use per assessment policy and IEP
exemplars.lre_statement: Pull-out SDI provides explicit reasoning instruction and guided practice that cannot be delivered with the pacing of the general classroom; the student remains in general education math for grade-level content and applies reasoning with scaffolds.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA math with extended time and chunking; calculator per policy. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Applied math reasoning regressed over the prior summer with slow recoupment; ESY math 2x/week for 45 minutes is proposed. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Pairs with the fifth-grade calculation goal to show vertical progression into reasoning.

exemplars.title: Grade 8 — SLD, written expression (multi-paragraph essays)
exemplars.profile_summary: An eighth-grade student with strong verbal reasoning who writes disorganized multi-paragraph essays with weak introductions, few transitions, and frequent syntax errors, scoring 2/6 on the state writing rubric.
strengths: Strong discussion skills and idea generation
Good use of evidence when prompted orally
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is worried about high school writing demands and asks for feedback strategies at home.
evaluation_data: Sentence-level: 60% of sentences complete; syntax errors in 4/10 sentences
Oral language: average to above average
Evaluation confirmed SLD in written expression

plaafp.academic: The student organizes ideas aloud but produces essays scoring 2/6, with weak thesis statements, missing transitions, and syntax errors. On-demand writing is harder than process writing; editing is minimal.
plaafp.functional: The student rushes through writing, avoids revising, and has trouble sustaining organization across paragraphs, affecting grades in all subjects that require writing.
plaafp.impact: Written-expression deficits related to the specific learning disability interfere with grade-level writing standards across content areas and with demonstrating knowledge on assessments.

goals.condition: Given a planning template and a familiar informational prompt
goals.skill: write a multi-paragraph essay with thesis, transitions, and conclusion
goals.measurement: District writing rubric with two trained raters

goals.area: Written expression — sentence structure and revision
goals.condition: Given a draft and an editing routine
goals.skill: revise to correct syntax, punctuation, and sentence boundaries
goals.target: 90% complete/correct sentences across 3 consecutive revised drafts

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with rubric-scored essays and revised drafts.
supplementary_aids_services: Essay planning templates and transition word banks
Model texts and rubrics in student-friendly language
Graphic organizers for evidence and reasoning
accommodations: Extended time on writing assignments and assessments
Speech-to-text or scribing when conventions are not the target
Use of word processor with spell/grammar check
exemplars.lre_statement: SDI in a resource setting provides explicit strategy instruction and guided revision; the student also receives push-in support during ELA writing to transfer skills. Pull-out is needed for focused sentence-level instruction and immediate feedback.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services and one push-in session (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district writing assessments with extended time, word processing, and speech-to-text as permitted. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed writing regression over the prior summer with slow recoupment of essay organization; ESY writing 2x/week, 45 minutes for 5 weeks is recommended. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Includes push-in service; validates the tool's mixed service delivery options.

exemplars.title: Grade 7 — SLD with executive function/study skills needs (functional goal)
exemplars.profile_summary: A seventh-grade student with SLD in reading who is failing classes primarily because of missing assignments, disorganized materials, and poor test preparation rather than skill deficits alone; homework completion is 45%.
strengths: Responds well to checklists and routines
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent says the student loses assignments and doesn't know what is due; evening homework causes daily conflict.
evaluation_data: Assignment accuracy: high when turned in
Team determined functional executive-function goals are needed alongside reading SDI

plaafp.academic: The student comprehends grade-7 text at 70% with scaffolds and performs well on completed work, but turns in only 45% of assignments and scores below proficient on tests due to incomplete preparation.
plaafp.functional: The student does not consistently record assignments, loses materials, and has no systematic study routine; organizational demands of seven classes exceed current skills.
plaafp.impact: Executive-function and study-skill needs associated with the specific learning disability interfere with demonstrating reading progress and with grades across all classes, requiring explicit organization/study instruction and a functional goal.

baselines.score: 1/4 tests prepared using a study plan

goals.area: Executive function — organization and assignment completion
goals.condition: Given a daily planner routine and adult check-ins
goals.skill: record assignments, organize materials, and submit work on time
goals.target: 85% completion and 5/5 prepared days across 4 consecutive weeks
goals.measurement: Gradebook audit and daily planner checks

goals.condition: Given a test calendar and a study-plan template
goals.skill: prepare for tests using distributed study sessions
goals.baseline: 1/4 tests prepared with a study plan
goals.target: 4/4 tests prepared with completed study plans across 6 weeks

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; weekly organization checks shared with parents through the planner.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Frustration and task avoidance are secondary to organization needs; executive-function supports are the primary intervention. If avoidance escalates, an FBA will be considered.
supplementary_aids_services: Set of classroom materials kept in the resource room
Weekly grade check with case manager
accommodations: Extended time on assignments and assessments
Reduced penalty for late work per district policy while organization goals are being taught
personnel_supports: Training for teachers on assignment-log checks
Coordination with counselor on grade checks
exemplars.lre_statement: The student receives reading SDI and executive-function instruction in a small setting to build independence; pull-out is needed to teach and practice organization routines with feedback. The student participates in all general education classes with organizational scaffolding.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA with extended time and chunking; district assessments with organizer use. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Organization routines showed significant regression over the summer with slow recoupment; ESY executive-function/study-skills sessions 2x/week for 30 minutes are proposed along with reading maintenance. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
source_lineage: Missouri DESE PLAAFP and SMART Goal rubrics
exemplars.notes: Shows a functional goal under SLD eligibility — a common tool gap; behavior support plan stays null until an FBA is done.
